name: BQ29330DBTR
title: 2- to 4-series-cell Li-ion / Li-polymer battery protection analog front end
summary: The bq29330 is a protection front end for battery packs of two, three or four Li-ion or Li-polymer cells in series. It drives N-channel charge and discharge FETs, turns them off on its own on discharge overload and on short circuit in charge or discharge with programmable thresholds and delays, and gives a host (such as a bq803x gas gauge) the individual cell, stack and pack voltages through a level-shifting amplifier. It has 2.5 V, 16 mA and 3.3 V, 25 mA regulators, a watchdog and power-on reset for the host, cell balancing switches, a thermistor drive and an I2C-compatible interface.

operation.text: Fed from VCC or BAT, this regulator holds about 3.3 V and is stable with 2.2 μF or more on its output. It has an internal current limit, typically 50 mA in normal operation. It powers LEDs, the 2.5 V regulator and the chip's own circuits. DSG and CHG stay low, FETs off, until it is up.
Fed from the 3.3 V LED rail, REG gives about 2.5 V, needs at least 1 μF to be stable and limits its current, typically to 50 mA in normal operation.

Out of shutdown, the part needs more than VSTARTUP on PACK to start its regulator. When REG has settled the regulator input moves over to VCC and keeps running from it. With VCC under its minimum operating voltage, removing the PACK supply stops the part. If VLED drops below roughly 2.3 V, the FETs turn off and REG, LEDOUT and TOUT and every other controllable function are disabled. At start CHG and DSG drive low (off) and ZVCHG drives low (on).

Overload watches for too much discharge current to protect the FETs, cells and series parts. A blanking delay runs before the FETs are turned off. OLV sets the threshold from 50 mV to 205 mV in 5 mV steps, default 50 mV; OLD sets the delay. RSNS = 1 halves the threshold, the step and the hysteresis.

operation.topic: Short circuit in charge and discharge
operation.text: Two further comparators catch severe current in the charge direction (SCC) and the discharge direction (SCD), each with its own blanking delay before the FETs go off. SCC and SCD registers each hold a threshold, 100 mV to 475 mV in 25 mV steps, and a delay. RSNS = 1 halves threshold, step and hysteresis.

The overload delay lets a brief current surge pass without cutting the load; it defaults to 1 ms and OLD sets 1 ms to 31 ms in 2 ms steps. The SCC and SCD delays default to 0 μs and run from 0 μs to 915 μs in 61 μs steps.

On an overload or short-circuit fault the FETs turn off, the matching STATUS bits (b0 to b3) set to 1 and XALERT goes low. The fault stays latched until the latch-clear bit is set and cleared. Turning a FET back on while the fault is still present sends the part straight back into protection.
For two cells, VC1 and VC2 are tied to VC3. For three cells, VC1 is tied to VC2.

Each series cell can be shifted down to a ground-referred voltage between CELL+ and CELL– for the host to read. The gain is 0.15 ± 0.003 and inverting, covering cells from 0 to 4.5 V. CELL_SEL b1:b0 picks the cell and b3:b2 the mode (cell, offset, reference).

The amplifier offset and gain can be calibrated by the host. Step 1: CAL1 = 1, CAL0 = 1, VMEN = 1; read VREF directly (trimmed to 0.975 V ±1%). Step 2: CAL1 = 0, CAL0 = 1, CELL1 = CELL0 = 0, VMEN = 1; read VOUT(4-5). Step 3: CAL1 = 1, CAL0 = 0, CELL1 = CELL0 = 0, VMEN = 1; read V(OUTR). Step 4: compute KACT. Step 5: compute VOS(ACT). Step 6: compute each cell voltage. For better accuracy the offset output is read for each cell in turn (CELL1:CELL0 = 01, 10, 11, with CAL1 = CAL0 = 0) giving VOUT(3-4), VOUT(2-3) and VOUT(1-2).
Setting PACK in FUNCTION_CONTROL puts PACK divided by 18 on CELL+, CELL–; setting BAT puts the VC1 stack voltage divided by 18 there. With both set, the stack (VC1) is shown.

Any one cell can be given a small bypass path so it takes less charge current, bringing cells to equal voltage. The bypass current is set by series resistors between the VC pins and the cell taps together with the internal switch (typically 400 Ω). CELL_SEL bits 4 to 7 choose the cell. Series resistors of 500 Ω to 1 kΩ are recommended. Absolute maximum balance current is 10 mA.
XALERT goes low on WDF, OL, SCC or SCD. It is released by toggling LTCLR 0 to 1 to 0 and then reading STATUS.
TOUT can switch REG onto a thermistor, typically 10 kΩ at 25°C. It is off by default to save power, is enabled by FUNCTION_CONTROL bit 3 and has at most 100 Ω output impedance.
The open-drain output sinks a 1 mA current-source drive and withstands up to 25 V. OUTPUT_CONTROL bit 4 turns it on; it is off by default.
Protection faults latch. Toggling LTCLR 0 to 1 to 0 releases the OL, SCC, SCD and WDF flags; the host can then drive the FETs through OUTPUT_CONTROL, and reading STATUS releases XALERT.
When REG comes up, XRST holds the host in reset for tRST so the 2.5 V rail can settle. On power-down XRST is asserted once REG is below 1.8 V. A watchdog fault also asserts XRST to restart the host.

WDI is the time base for the fault delays and feeds the watchdog. After tRST, if no host clock arrives within tWDTINT, CHG, DSG and ZVCHG turn off and XRST is asserted. Once running, a gap of tWDWT with no clock counts as a stopped oscillator, with the same result. WDF stays set after the clock returns until it is cleared through LTCLR. The watchdog keeps running in sleep mode. With WDRST = 1 the reset is pulsed on each 500 ms timeout; with WDRST = 0 it is not.

An OL, SCC or SCD event turns off DSG or CHG according to current direction. The host can switch the FETs on or off through OUTPUT_CONTROL only where the protection logic permits, and not during initialisation; they default off. The CHG driver can run from PACK and the DSG driver from BAT. When the part powers down the gate drivers fall to GND and the FETs turn off.

Chargers with and without a precharge phase are supported, and a cell stack at 0 V can be charged. The charge FET must be on to pass current; with the battery near 0 V, PACK sits near the battery voltage and is too low to run the part. With PMS tied to PACK, PMS_CHG lets CHG connect to PACK for 0 V charging.

Three modes: normal, sleep and ship. Sleep turns the FETs off and stops overload and short-circuit detection while keeping the cell amplifier, GPOD, balancing and watchdog. Ship shuts everything down including REG and the I2C interface, and register contents are lost; it is entered when SHIP is set and PACK carries no supply, and left when PACK is powered again. A voltage above VSTARTUP on PACK brings the part out of shutdown into normal mode.

The part is an I2C-compatible slave on SDATA and SCLK and never drives the clock; the host may use an I2C port or GPIO. The 7-bit address is 0100 000 (0x20): write byte 0x40, read byte 0x41. A write is address, register, data. A read is address and register, then a repeated start (protocol A) or stop and start (protocol B), address with read bit, and one data byte answered with NACK. There is no general call (a NACK may come back) and no address auto-increment; the same register can be read or written again without resending its address. Clock up to 100 kHz.
The DBT package is a 30-lead TSSOP, 1.2 mm maximum height, following JEDEC MO-153. Dimensions are in millimetres; values in parentheses are reference only.
